title: Billing Office Rules for Delivery Pass Subscriptions: Activation, Billing Cycles, Past-Due Status and Lapse
content:
These rules govern the subscription side of every Delivery & Pickup Services plan.

## Rules in force

1. **Activation.** A plan activates on its trial end date, which is the enrollment date plus the plan's free-trial days; with a free trial of 0 days the trial end date is the enrollment date itself.
2. **Billing cycles.** Each billing cycle lasts the plan's billing-cycle number of calendar months, with the month-end falling back to the last day of a shorter month.
3. **One charge per cycle.** Each cycle is charged once: a plan whose fee ledger already shows a subscription charge for a given cycle start date is not charged for that cycle again.
4. **Past due.** A subscription charge that cannot be collected puts the plan past due, and the date the charge failed is recorded on the plan as its past-due date.
5. **Grace period.** A past-due plan whose fee is collected no later than the date the charge failed plus the past-due grace days, counted in calendar days with the failure date as day 0, returns to active; otherwise it lapses on the next day.
6. **Plans without a subscription.** Plans without a subscription never go past due.

## Clauses no longer in force

- *"A plan with a subscription fee above 0.00 is charged that fee for its first cycle on activation and for every later cycle on the cycle's first day."* This clause is **no longer in force**; the amount charged for a Delivery Pass billing cycle is set by the current subscription charging basis for Delivery & Pickup Services, which supersedes it.
- *"While past due, where plan prices stop applying while past due, orders are priced as Kestrel Pay-Per-Delivery orders."* This clause is **no longer in force**; the pricing of an order placed while its plan is past due is set by the current order-fee basis, which supersedes it.

## The grace period in calendar days

The clock starts on the date the charge failed, as the plan's past-due date shows it, and that date is day 0. The last day on which collection returns the plan to active is day N, where N is the plan's past-due grace days; collection on day N itself is in time. A plan still unpaid at the end of day N lapses on day N plus 1.

| Plan | Grace days | Charge failed (day 0) | Last day to collect (in time) | Lapses on, if unpaid |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Kestrel Delivery Pass Monthly | 7 | 1 May | 8 May | 9 May |
| Kestrel Senior Delivery Pass | 7 | 20 August | 27 August | 28 August |
| Kestrel Delivery Pass Annual | 14 | 1 May | 15 May | 16 May |

Hypothetical boundary cases on Kestrel Delivery Pass Monthly with a charge that failed on 1 May: the fee collected on 8 May returns the plan to active; the fee not collected by the end of 8 May leaves the plan to lapse on 9 May.

## Points of reference

**Can Kestrel Pay-Per-Delivery go past due?** No. It has no subscription, and plans without a subscription never go past due.

**When does a Kestrel Delivery Pass Monthly enrolled on 2 March activate?** On its trial end date, 2 March plus 30 days, which is 1 April.
